macranhinga:eswiki:6.title: Macranhinga (Características y reconstrucción de hábitos de vida)

facts.statement: The genus Macranhinga was described by Noriega in 1992.
The type species M. paranensis was described based on complete tarsometatarsi and other skeletal parts.
facts.quote: The type species is M. paranensis, which was described on the basis of complete tarsometatarsi and several dissociated skeletal elements.

facts.statement: Specimens of M. paranensis were found in the Ituzaingó Formation along the Paraná River in northeastern Argentina.
facts.quote: All the specimens come from the Ituzaingó Formation that crops out discontinuously along the eastern cliffs of the Paraná River in northeastern Argentina

facts.statement: The species M. ranzii was originally described from the Solimões Formation in Acre, Brazil.
facts.quote: A second species, M. ranzii was described from the Solimões Formation in Acre, Amazonian Brazil

facts.statement: Macranhinga is an extinct genus of darters in the family Anhingidae.
facts.quote: Macranhinga is a genus of extinct darters belonging to the Anhingidae.

facts.statement: Macranhinga was much larger than any other known fossil or living anhinga.
facts.quote: The most striking feature of this bird is its large size, much greater than in all other known fossil or extant anhingas.

facts.statement: The genera Meganhinga and Giganhinga are synonyms of Macranhinga.
facts.quote: synonyms: Meganhinga Alvarenga, 1995 Giganhinga Rinderknetch & Noriega, 2002

facts.statement: The genus Macranhinga was originally described in 1992 by paleontologist Jorge Ignacio Noriega.
facts.quote: El género Macranhinga fue descrito originalmente en el año 1992 por el paleontólogo Jorge Ignacio Noriega

facts.statement: M. chilensis lived from the early to middle Miocene in central-southern Chile.
facts.quote: Macranhinga chilensis (Alvarenga, 1995) Del Mioceno inferior a medio del centro-sur de Chile.

facts.statement: M. kiyuensis lived from the Pliocene to the middle Pleistocene in Uruguay.
facts.quote: Macranhinga kiyuensis (Rinderknetch & Noriega, 2002) Del Plioceno-Pleistoceno medio del Uruguay.

facts.statement: M. paranensis lived from the late Miocene to the early Pliocene in Entre Ríos province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Macranhinga paranensis Noriega, 1992 Del Mioceno superior al Plioceno inferior de la provincia de Entre Ríos, nordeste de la Argentina.

facts.statement: M. ranzii lived from the late Miocene to the early Pliocene in Acre, Brazil, and Entre Ríos, Argentina.
facts.quote: Macranhinga ranzii Alvarenga & Guilherme, 2003 Del Mioceno superior-Plioceno inferior del río Acre, en el estado de Acre, Brasil, y de la provincia de Entre Ríos, nordeste de la Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Meganhinga was described in 1995 by Herculano M. F. Alvarenga for the species M. chilensis from Chile.
facts.quote: Meganhinga fue descrito en el año 1995 por Herculano M. F. Alvarenga para incluir a su nueva especie, recuperada del Mioceno inferior de Chile: Meganhinga chilensis.

facts.statement: Macranhinga species weighed between approximately 5.8 kg and 18.4 kg.
facts.quote: Las especies de Macranhinga poseían pesos de entre unos 5,8 kg y unos 18,4 kg.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Macranhinga performed long, deep dives to catch large fish and prey.
facts.quote: Habrían realizado prolongados y profundos buceos para capturar peces y otras presas (bastante grandes en comparación con las actuales aningas)

facts.statement: Macranhinga likely competed for food resources with dolphins, caimans, and seals.
facts.quote: compitiendo por el mismo recurso con delfines, cocodrílidos (gaviálidos) y pinnípedos.

facts.statement: The larger species of Macranhinga are thought to have completely lost the ability to fly.
facts.quote: Por lo menos las especies mayores se cree que habrían perdido totalmente la capacidad de volar

facts.statement: Macranhinga likely nested on the ground of small islands and islets, behaving similarly to modern large penguins.
facts.quote: habrían anidado sobre el suelo de pequeñas islas e islotes, presentando hábitos similares a los actuales grandes pingüinos.

facts.statement: Macranhinga fossils date from the Aquitanian to the Zanclean stages, between 23.04 and 5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Zanclean (23.04 to 5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: A 2015 review determined that Macranhinga is a valid genus containing four species.
rejected.quote: La conclusión de la revisión sistemática determinó que Macranhinga es un género válido, al que se adscriben 4 especies

rejected.statement: The genus Giganhinga was described in 2002 by Rinderknetch and Noriega for the species M. kiyuensis from Uruguay.
rejected.quote: Giganhinga fue descrito en el año 2002 por Rinderknetch y Jorge Ignacio Noriega, para incluir una nueva especie recuperada del Mioceno de Uruguay: Giganhinga kiyuensis.
rejected.reason: species not named so in the source: ['M. kiyuensis']
